subject: Re: Urgent: NovaSys regional latency & errors in us-west-2 — immediate routing ask
messages:
From: Emily Chen <emily.chen@novasys.com>
To: vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai
Cc: carlos.m@novasys.com, support@novasys.com
Date: Thu, 09 Dec 2027 16:07:00 -0800
Subject: Sudden latency & 502s in us-west-2 impacting NovaSys real-time features

Vivek / Redwood team,

We started seeing a sharp increase in p50/p95 latency and 502 errors against your us-west-2 endpoints starting ~15:55 PST (attached sample logs). Our real-time personalization pipelines are failing enrichment calls and falling back to cached stubs — user impact is visible in product dashboards. Key symptoms:
- p50 from ~40ms to ~350ms, p95 to ~1.2s
- 502 and 5xx spike ~12% of requests for the last 12 minutes
- Throughput holding steady but error amplification on long-context calls

This is causing user-facing errors for high-value customers. We need a temporary routing diversion to a healthy region (us-east-1) and confirmation that you can pin a compatible model variant there (we use rwd-large in us-west-2). Please advise:
1) Can you initiate a cross-region route shift now and what ETA?
2) Any quality delta we should expect if you roll to a different variant (quantized / smaller model)?
3) Please assign an incident owner and provide a PagerDuty incident id.

If possible we need an exec-level contact for credits/SLA discussion.

Attached: novasys-error-sample-1209.log

— Emily Chen
CTO, NovaSys
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Chen <emily.chen@novasys.com>
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.ai, jordan_blake@redwood.ai, rachel_kim@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 09 Dec 2027 16:15:30 -08:00
Subject: Re: Sudden latency & 502s in us-west-2 impacting NovaSys real-time features

Emily — thanks for the heads up and the logs. We opened PD-87231 and assigned an incident commander (Jordan Blake). Initial telemetry shows a KV-cache saturation signature plus a downstream encoder timeout cluster coincident with a model hot-shard.

Immediate actions we're taking (ETA in parentheses):
- Initiating manual routing diversion to us-east-1 (start: now, full blue/green switch by ~16:28 PST).
- Standing up a pinned rwd-medium (quantized) variant in us-east-1 to accept traffic while we stabilize rwd-large in us-west-2 (quality delta: medium - minor difference on long-form tokenization; expect identical short answers, ~2-5% perplexity increase on benchmarks).
- Enabling prefix-KV sticky caching to reduce rehydration pressure (rolling within 5 mins).

Monica, Jordan — can you coordinate the cutover play and confirm routing weights and canary size? Jordan, please post the exact runbook step IDs and the link to the routing change once live.

Emily, we'll keep you tight. I'll also prepare a short executive summary and loop in our head of Customer Success for the credit conversation.

Attachments: initial-impact-summary.pdf
PagerDuty: https://redwood.pagerduty.com/incidents/PD-87231
Runbook ref: RB-serve-011A

— Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
To: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Cc: rachel_kim@redwood.ai, emily.chen@novasys.com
Date: Thu, 09 Dec 2027 16:21:10 -08:00
Subject: Re: Sudden latency & 502s in us-west-2 impacting NovaSys real-time features

On Thu, Dec 9, 2027 at 16:15, Vivek Kulkarli <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Initial telemetry shows a KV-cache saturation signature plus a downstream encoder timeout cluster coincident with a model hot-shard.

Action log (live):
1) Started manual routing diversion at 16:18 PST — initial 10% traffic to us-east-1 (canary).
2) Observing canary: p50 ~48ms, p95 ~220ms, 5xx ~0.5% on canary at 16:22 PST. Positive signal.
3) Gradual ramping to 50% over next 6 mins (will pause if 5xx > 2% or p95 > 1s).
4) Pinned rwd-medium-quant (model variant tag: rwd-medium-q-v3) in us-east-1; loading KV prefixes for NovaSys to reduce cold starts.
5) Backend fix: increasing encoder socket timeout from 2s -> 5s for affected shard (temporary).

Notes:
- The quality tradeoff on rwd-medium-q-v3 vs rwd-large: some long-hallucination cases differ; we recommend keeping a short canonical prompt that avoids extended chains while we normalize state in us-west-2.
- Runbook step IDs executed: RB-serve-011A (diversion), RB-cache-004C (KV preload), RB-telemetry-002 (safety gates).

I'll post the routing change link and metrics snapshot in PD.

— Jordan Blake
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

> On Thu, Dec 9, 2027 at 16:07, Emily Chen <emily.chen@novasys.com> wrote:
> > This is causing user-facing errors for high-value customers. We need a temporary routing diversion...

From: Emily Chen <emily.chen@novasys.com>
To: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Cc: carlos.m@novasys.com, cfo@novasys.com
Date: Thu, 09 Dec 2027 17:24:05 -08:00
Subject: Re: Sudden latency & 502s in us-west-2 impacting NovaSys real-time features

Vivek / Jordan / Monica —

Thank you for the rapid response and the diversion. We validated initial canary traffic and are seeing restored user flows for the impacted features. Two quick asks while you stabilize:
1) Can you escalate this internally to the executive team for a formal SLA/credit discussion? Please include your Head of Customer Success and someone from finance.
2) We need a post-incident report covering root cause analysis, timeline, mitigation steps, and an action item list with owners.

We appreciate the speed. We'll keep monitoring and will send metrics from our side (I've attached a short sample).

Attachments: novasys-impact-sample-1209.csv

— Emily Chen
CTO, NovaSys
